title: SAE Feature Steering Side-Effects: Single-Feature Ablation Collateral

original_idea.body:
# SAE Feature Steering Side-Effects: Single-Feature Ablation Collateral

**Problem:** Ablating one SAE latent may degrade unrelated capabilities due to absorption/superposition; collateral damage is rarely measured against a control.

**Direction:** Using a pretrained GPT-2-small SAE, clamp several interpreted features to zero and measure the intended change plus collateral (perplexity, unrelated-task accuracy). Compare against clamping a random/dead latent.

**Why it matters:** Feature steering is proposed as a safety lever; quantifying collateral damage tells the community whether SAE steering is deployment-safe.

**Relevant context:** Golden Gate Claude lineage; absorption/superposition (Chanin et al. 2024).

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped precision-vs-collateral scatter with random/dead-latent control.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Deployment-safety of a public interp lever labs deprioritize; third-party-useful.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference over public GPT-2-small SAE; low compute.

novelty.reasoning: Feature-steering side-effects noted qualitatively; a controlled collateral measurement may be partly open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Feature-steering side-effects noted qualitatively; a controlled collateral-damage measurement may be partly open.
